page.layout: One printed page of running text, no margin notes. Running head centred at the top. Catchword at the lower right.

p.i: petrari: ut, etsi tum, cùm in manum est calamus sumendus, ad ea non confu-giamus, non tamen male inepteque scri-bamus: veluti concitato nauigio, etiam remorum impetu atque pulsu remisso, nauim nihilominus suum retinere cur-sum: propter contractum iam habitum sine singulorum modorum obseruatio-ne, scite Musicos modulari: carmen con-dere bonum Poetas videmus, qui pue-rorum more in syllabis examinandis non sunt occupati? Nam ad Rhetori-ca præcepta quod attinet, licet illorum in epistolis exarandis usum esse ma-gnum inficias nemo ire queat: tamen & hoc haud, opinor, grauatè omnes conce-dent [illegible, ~8 letters], obseruatione adhibi-ta, non pauca reperiri, quæ Epistola-rum sunt propria, & neque ad oratio-nes referri possunt, neque à dicendi ma-gistris in rhetoricis traduntur. page.notes: The Greek word after "concedent" is printed in Greek letters but is not legible enough to transcribe; it is marked illegible. The catchword "go" at the lower right is read as "go" (probably the start of "ergo", the next page). The running head is read as PRAEFATIO. Long s has been normalised to s and the u/v spelling corrected per the rules, but the Greek and the ampersand-type sign after "tamen" and "&" were copied as seen.
